title: Baseball by the Numbers
text:
This site explores more than a century of Major League Baseball history using records from the Lahman Baseball Database. Across the league as a whole, raw season home-run totals appear to suffer sudden collapses in years like 1981, 1994, and 2020—until we account for shortened schedules. Measuring home runs per team-game smooths away those artificial dips and reveals a dramatic long-term climb from the Dead-Ball Era to today’s power-first game.
Zooming in on individual hitters tells a parallel story about eras and power. Nine of the fifteen players with the most career home runs in MLB history were active during the 1994–2009 Steroid Era, led by all-time king Barry Bonds (762 career home runs), whose late-career surge peaked at 73 home runs in 2001. Use the Home runs and Sluggers links in the navigation bar above to explore the full charts and analyses.
